subject: Renewal review + proposed bakeoff window (Gridline)
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@gridline.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@gridline.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T14:22:00Z
Subject: Renewal timeline + initial bakeoff requirements

Hi Naomi/Ben/Karthik,

Quick note — our annual contract with Redwood is up in early September and procurement has asked us to run a short bakeoff to validate price and performance ahead of signing. At this point the two asks are:

- Performance: we need end-to-end 95th percentile generation latency under 300ms for our core inference path at 75 concurrent sessions.
- Cost: show a comparative per-token cost for a sustained 100k tokens/day workload over a 30-day projection.

I attached a short PDF with the bakeoff constraints and the procurement checklist (Gridline-bakeoff-requirements.pdf). Exact dates are still flexible but procurement would like a live window between Aug 10–14 if possible.

We'd also like to understand whether you can guarantee a Dedicated-capacity commitment for the trial or whether we'd need to rely on hosted tier with priority routing. FYI there is some interest in AzureServe from our infra team as a fallback; they asked us to benchmark alternatives.

Can we schedule a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow to lock the scope?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering
Gridline AI

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@gridline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T17:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline + initial bakeoff requirements

Tom — thanks for the heads up and the PDF. I pulled the team in to start scoping. Short answers up front: we can run an isolated Dedicated pool for the bakeoff and we'll provide a comparative cost projection.

Next steps I'm proposing:
1) Internal alignment at Redwood today (30m) — Ben and Karthik to confirm test harness and required telemetry.
2) Share a lightweight benchmark plan with you by EOD Wednesday (I'll attach a concise runbook).
3) Book the live window Aug 11–12 as a first preference; we'll mark Aug 13 as a fallback.

Can you confirm whether procurement needs any additional security artifacts (SOC2 attestation, audit logs) in the bakeoff package? I can include them in the runbook.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal Account Executive | Redwood Inference

>

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:15:00Z
Subject: Redwood proposed bench plan + telemetry

Naomi/Karthik — draft bench plan below. I kept it tight so we can get it into Gridline's hands quickly.

Overview:
- Test harness: replay of 6 canonical user flows (attached: redwood-bench-plan.md) using the same prompt mix and session distribution Gridline provided.
- Load pattern: step to 75 concurrent sessions, hold for 30 minutes, spike to 120 for 2 minutes.
- Metrics captured: token latency (per-token and end-to-end), p99 latency, memory/KV cache hit rates, GPU utilization, and per-token cost estimate (we'll simulate expected steady-state).
- Environment: Dedicated pool (4x A100-equivalent slices) provisioned for exclusive use for bakeoff window.

Attachments I will produce:
- bench-runner Docker image tag (stub)
- bench-instructions.yaml (runbook)
- perf-collector config for traces

Open questions:
- Does Gridline want us to run the benchmark on their VPC (private) or using our hosted region in us-west-2? Private VPC would require a short network onboarding, hosted is faster.

I'll bundle these into a single runbook and share by COB.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Amelia Park <amelia.park@gridline.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@gridline.ai>, procurement@gridline.ai
Date: 2026-08-03T14:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal timeline + initial bakeoff requirements

Thanks Naomi/Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement confirmed SOC2 is required for the final contract but for the bakeoff they only need proof-of-attestation + audit-log availability. I'll attach the procurement checklist separately.

We prefer the test on our VPC if possible — security wants to see network isolation. Can you provide a brief network onboarding checklist? We can open a Jira ticket and our infra team will stand up the necessary peering.

Regarding AzureServe, I can't share internal vendor discussions, but procurement has asked us to include one alternate vendor in the scoring matrix. The infra team will run their own validation; our goal is to validate Redwood's performance and operational fit.

Available slots for the live run: Aug 11 (15:00–17:00 EDT) or Aug 12 (10:00–12:00 EDT). Either works for us if you can provision Dedicated capacity.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Park
Product Ops Manager
Gridline AI

Subject: Re: Renewal timeline + initial bakeoff requirements

Team — looped in. Quick operational guidance from leadership:

1) If Gridline requests Dedicated for the bakeoff, approve it — we should treat this as a short-term capacity reservation (2–3 days) charged to a trial cost center.
2) Offer provisional price protection for 90 days post-signing if they move to a 12-month committed Dedicated contract (small standard % credit). We can use that as a leverage during the bakeoff.
3) Prepare a canary rollback plan and a fallback to a lighter quantized model variant in case of perf regressions.

Ben/Naomi — please prepare a one-page save plan that includes: the bench runbook summary, provisional pricing slide, and the operational checklist for the VPC onboard. We'll attach this to the commercial SOW. Deal ID RDW-4597.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Amelia/Tom — thanks for the alignment. Attached is our concise save plan and the runbook (bench-instructions.yaml) plus a draft SOW that includes the provisional price protection language. High-level summary: 

1) Bench approach: run the bench on Gridline VPC (we'll coordinate peering); target window Aug 11 15:00–17:00 EDT. Redwood will provision a Dedicated pool isolated for the run. Bench plan attached.
2) Operational guarantees: we will supply SOC2 summary, audit-log access for the trial, and a canary rollback + fallback model variant (quantized) if required.
3) Commercial: provisional price protection for 90 days post-signing if Gridline commits to a 12-month Dedicated reservation (terms summary in SOW).
4) Next steps:
   - Gridline: confirm formal acceptance of Aug 11 window and provide VPC peering contact (Jira ticket preferred).
   - Redwood: finalize bench runner image and perf collection config; share DocuSign link for an addendum SOW (link below).

Attachments: bench-instructions.yaml, sow-redwood-gridline-v1.docx
DocuSign (SOW addendum): https://app.docusign.com/some-ds-link/sow-gridline
Drive runbook folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-gridline-bakeoff

I'll stand on the scheduling once you confirm. Looking forward to demonstrating the end-to-end latency and cost story.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Principal Account Executive | Redwood Inference
